Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Commander in Chief of the EFF Julius Malema has made it clear the will be contesting the 2019 elections along racial lines: What does this mean for SA?

Unique Selling Point:
This past weekend Julius Malema was quoted as saying he was going after Nelson Mandela Bay mayor Athol Trollip specifically because he is white. "Cutting the throat of whiteness" in this way is according to Malema the only way to make people sit up and notice. Is this the end of an already shaky EFF/DA alliance in some of the major metros, or will it play into the hands of the ANC by weakening what many have described as a "pay as you go" alliance. More importantly, does this kind of commentary not fall under hate speech, and could stoking such racial sentiments not lead us down the path of violence and revolution?

Press Release:



The Economic Freedom Fighters
They’re loud and abrasive and they’ve been disrupting South African politics since their inception. From pushing Jacob Zuma to pay back the money, free higher education and a constitutional amendment to allow for land expropriation without compensation – the Economic Freedom Fighters, are credited with changing the country’s political landscape. Carte Blanche analyses a political party on the rise.


Script:


EFF
8 March 2018

Voice
This week firebrand Julius Malema made headlines once again after he said on sunday that he was going after the mayor of Nelson Mandela Bay, Athol Trollip's, job.

Sound Up Malema
Why not Mashaba? Why not Solly? Because the mayor of DA in PE is a white man. So these people if you want to hit them hard, go after a white man. They feel a terrible pain, because you have touched a white man.

Voice
That wasn’t the only reason the EFF were at the center of attention though. The party also managed to force the ANC’s hand and push through land expropriation without compensation.

Link Macfarlane
The EFF successfully managed to gain the ANC’s backing in parliament in their motion to change the constitution, and allow the government to expropriate land without compensation. Only time will tell how the two parties different ideologies on the land issue will play out, but one thing is certain, the move has a lot of South Africans, very nervous.

Voice
On tuesday the Zulu king, Goodwill Zwelenthini, vowed to protect his land - administered by the Ingonyama Trust - and called on all Zulus to help him in the fight. But the always brazen Malema hit back at the king during a press conference on thursday, a move not many South African Politicians would make.

Sound Up Malema
We love the Zulu king by the way, we support him, we gave him cattle. But we can disagree with him, and we should do that. We should do that. There are no holy cows in this country. We must debate issues openly, including disagreeing with the Zulu king.

Link Macfarlane
Love him or hate him, Julius Malema has proven to be a gifted politician and a charismatic leader. His promise of economic emancipation for the poor and down trodden has garnered wide spread support. And far from shying away from controversy, the commander in chief of the Economic Freedom Fighters seems instead to have thrived on it.

Voice
From his memorable tirades in parliament…

Sound Up Julius Malema
Julius: When are you paying the money?
EFF members: PAy back the money, pay back the money!

Voice
To leading thousands in marches on the Union Buildings.

Sound Up Malema
Because when we are united, we will never be defeated by an illiterate president.

Voice
Political analyst Professor Mcebisi Ndletyana says Malema appeals to a specific constituency.

Sound Up Prof Mcebisi Ndletyana
So it’s a combination of both charisma and idealogical resonance. What they say resonates with unhappy, disgruntled people. Especially young people who are battling to find jobs. And also people that feel that the current status quo does not speak to them, people in the informal settlements for instance.

Sound Up Julius Malema(singing)
Shoot to kill… Shoot to kill…

Voice
The question is often asked whether Malema’s radical ideology and militant political rhetoric might not one day lead to violence and bloodshed on a national scale. Professor Ndletyana says that might very well be the case if we can’t fix the inequalities we still face as a nation.

Sound Up Prof Ndletyana
This is not rocket science, it is not rocket science. In a situation where there is injustice, and people are waiting for redress, if they don’t get that redress, if they see the former perpetrators benefitting, in a society that is meant to be equal, their anger and resentment grows, and at some point there will be an implosion. It’s basic common sense.

Link Macfarlane
Throughout his colourful career Julius Malema has often changed his opinions on a variety of issues, not least of wich his undying support and later disgust for former president Jacob Zuma. But with his arch enemy and main political draw card out of the picture, how will the EFF remain relevant?

Voice
Mari Harris is the public affairs director at market research company IPSOS. They conduct bi-annual polls on some of South Africa’s leading political parties. One of the data points they research is a trust score, as given to parties by their own supporters.

Sound Up Mari Harris
The supporters of the DA and the EFF have far more trust in their parties, it’s in the 80 percents, than what the ANC supporters have.

Voice
The data also shows that EFF supporters are in general a lot younger than DA or ANC voters.

Sound Up Mari
In fact almost 70% of the EFF supporters are younger than 35, they want to vote for change, they want a say in government, and they have a very strong support for Julius Malema.

Voice
Professor Ndletyana says it’s this demographic who will keep the EFF going.

Sound Up Ndletyana
And so long as the ANC and the broader society doesn’t adress that, there will continue to be relevance for parties like Julius Malema’s. Not so much because they fabricate the disgruntlement, no they don’t fabricate it, it’s there, they are just giving it articulation.

Link Macfarlane
From their organisation’s name to the millitary ranks bestowed upon high level officials, the EFF’s approach to politics is certainly militant. But in a country still struggling to deal with an opressive past, is this the answer to South Africa’s problems?

Voice
Malema also had this to say on the Trollip issue.

Sound Up Malema
But we are starting with this whiteness, we are cutting the throat of whiteness.

Voice
We met the CEO of the South African Human Rights Commision, Advocate Tseliso Thipanyane, at a conference he was speaking at in Sandton this week.

Sound Up Thipanyane
The Human Rights Commission have received over 17 complaints around the remarks made by Julius Malema. And we’ll be looking at the issues raised and whether his remarks do constitute a violation of section 16 of our constitution in terms of hate speech, or if they do constitute a violation of the Equality act in terms of the remarks being hurtful

Voice
In thursday’s press conference, Malema backtracked on his earlier comments about Athol Trollip, saying they were punishing the DA for not backing the land expropriation resolution.

Sound Up Julius Malema
We therefore took a decision to pass a motion of no - confidence in the mayor of Nelson Mandela Bay, because he is the national leader of the DA. He presided over a decision which will perpetuate white supremacy and continue to exploit our people, particularly the landless masses of our people.

Voice
Thipanyane says he cannot comment on the outcome of the investigation until it has been concluded, but urges politicians, even if they are speaking within the confines of the law, to consider their words carefully.

Sound Up Thipanyane
You could act within the confines of the law, but still cause some pain and hurt elsewhere. And the issue is that really what you want, what are the values of nation building?

Voice
Thipanyane says the commission supports the land expropriation resolution, but that they will be keeping a close eye on the process.

Sound Up Thipanyane
African people make up about 70% of the population but certainly they don’t own 70% of the land. But also how then we address the issue of land, we should do it in such a manner that we don’t destroy the country, we move forward as a country and we promote unity and a cohesive society.

Voice
Ultimately it will be government, and not the EFF, who have control over land reform. How much of a part the EFF will play in the matter will be determined by how much support the they receive in the 2019 elections.

Link Macfarlane
Since the last round of local government elections, the EFF have been in the enviable position of playing kingmakers to several political parties. But those days may be numbered as they face a revived ANC under the leadership of President Cyril Ramaphosa in the national elections next year.

Voice
And as the ANC’s so called new era dawns, it will be interesting to see if the EFF can muster the same kind of support they had in 2014. If the polls are to be believed, many South Africans don’t feel like any political parties truly represent them.


Sound Up Mari
About half of South Africans say there’s not really a political party currently that express their views.

Voice
And although the surveys do indicate a renewed faith in government after the election of Cyril Ramaphosa as president, that has not translated into numbers for the ANC just yet.

Sound Up Mari
What we see up to now is not necessarily those people who stayed away for instance in 2016, not necessarily streaming back to the ANC. A lot of people say let’s wait and see.

Voice
And while the still deeply divided ruling party gets it’s house in order, Malema, speaking at a press conference on thursday, seemed to have few more Aces up his sleeve.

Sound Up Malema
We told you that we are going to lead through superior logic. Leadership doesn’t always mean you must occupy the front seat. You can lead from behind. How do you lead from behind? You lead through ideas.







PROMOS

Promo 1

Voice
Punishing the DA and land expropriation without compensation - firebrand Julius Malema in the spotlight

Sound Up Malema
But we are starting with this whiteness, we are cutting the throat of whiteness.



Promo 2

Voice
Julius Malema’s plans for land expropriation without compensation lead to a war of words with the king of the Zulus.

Sound Up Malema
There are no holy cows in this country. We must debate issues openly, including disagreeing with the Zulu king.


Promo 10 sec

Voice
The successful resolution in parliament to allow land expropriation without compensation, saw EFF Commander in Chief Julius Malema in the spotlight again this week.
